title: Sage and thyme steam for sinus congestion
subtitle: A facial steam of Salvia officinalis and Thymus vulgaris for blocked sinuses and head colds
excerpt: Sage and thyme steam is a bowl of just-boiled water with a handful of each herb, inhaled under a towel for 5 to 10 minutes to clear blocked sinuses and ease the head-pressure of a cold. The volatile oils in both herbs, thymol, carvacrol, and the eucalyptol-adjacent compounds in sage, are antimicrobial and decongestant. One session per day during acute congestion. Not for children under 12 years.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), sage and thyme entries, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Thymus vulgaris L. (2012) and Salvia officinalis L. (2016), EMA open access monographs.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried herbs store 12 months in a sealed tin. Prepare each session fresh.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation that reduces swelling in the nasal and sinus mucous membranes to open blocked passages. Herbal steam decongestants work by direct inhalation of volatile oils, which reduce inflammation and help loosen mucus.

content.text: Sage and thyme steam is a large bowl of just-boiled water with a generous handful of each dried herb, inhaled under a towel for 5 to 10 minutes. A traditional

preparation for blocked sinuses, sinus pressure, and the head-heaviness of a cold. The aromatic oils in both herbs, thymol and carvacrol from the thyme, camphor and eucalyptol-adjacent compounds from the sage, are carried directly to the sinus mucosa on the steam, reducing swelling and loosening congestion. One session per day at the worst of the cold.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place the dried sage and thyme in a large heatproof bowl. Pour 1 litre of just-boiled water over the herbs. Allow to stand for 1 minute.
Lean over the bowl at a comfortable distance, 25 to 30 cm above the water, and drape a large towel over your head and the bowl to trap the steam.
Breathe slowly and deeply through your nose for 5 to 10 minutes. Come up for fresh air if the steam feels too intense.
Blow your nose gently after the session. Keep warm for 30 minutes afterwards to allow the airways to settle.
Once daily during acute sinus congestion. Use on the first two or three days of a cold for best effect.
Dried sage and thyme each store 12 months in a sealed tin. Prepare the steam fresh for each session.
When not to use this remedy
Do not use if you have asthma. See a doctor for sinus symptoms that last more than 10 days, are accompanied by facial pain and fever (possible sinusitis), or are comes with any neurological symptoms.
